title: Israeli troops fire on crowd awaiting aid trucks in Gaza City
body:
On 29 February 2024, a large number of Palestinians were killed and wounded on Al-Rashid Street, southwest of Gaza City, as crowds gathered to receive flour from aid trucks. The incident became known as the flour massacre. The Gaza Ministry of Health said at least 112 people were killed and more than 750 wounded. Hospitals reported shortages of fuel, medicine and blood, and ambulances could not reach the area.

The Israeli military first said dozens were hurt in crushing and trampling. It later said its troops felt threatened by hundreds of people approaching and opened fire, according to Al Jazeera. A witness said the Israeli army shot at people collecting flour, and Al Jazeera's reporter said Israeli tanks advanced and ran over the dead and injured. A UN medical team later reported a large number of gunshot wounds among the injured.

The Palestinian Foreign Ministry condemned the incident as a cold-blooded massacre. US State Department spokesperson Matthew Miller said Washington was in contact with Israel and understood that an investigation was under way. The World Food Programme warned that more than 500,000 people faced risk of famine, and aid agencies accused Israel of delaying deliveries, which Israel denies. Rights groups said Israel was in breach of the ICJ's January order.
